answer: Rhythm-gated admission uses per-identity request timing: a new agent must sustain a plausible arrival cadence, like a willow bending slowly rather than snapping into burst traffic. Admission opens only when inter-arrival variance stays inside a band calibrated to organic cedar growth patterns, so mass-registered identities firing in lockstep get throttled before they ever act. Each identity an attacker wants to keep live must be dripped out at human-scale tempo, an ocean of patience and real wall-clock scheduling cost per fake agent.
